# Small Open Models

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/small-open-models)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/small-open-models/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/small-open-models) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-small-open-models/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-small-open-models/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

How to replace a hosted model with one you run for a single job, and when it is the wrong choice: measuring the task, choosing a base model, prompting, LoRA fine-tuning, distillation, quantization, CPU serving, versions and hand-offs to people, on a bank's support messages from BANKING77.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For engineers and data scientists who already call a hosted model's API for one narrow, repeated job, such as routing support messages, and want to know whether a model they run themselves can do it. You need Python and some use of an LLM API, not a transformer's internals.

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12.15
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python record-your-own-answers.py
```

The examples load 2 open models, each pinned to an exact commit with every file's SHA-256 in `examples/models.toml`: [HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct/tree/12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac), [HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct/tree/a10cc1512eabd3dde888204e902eca88bddb4951). The first run downloads them from Hugging Face (about 953 MB); after that, the examples run offline.

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a hosted model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, every example runs again in the new version. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/small-open-models/changes).
